# Generalised chart-export framework — test sandbox

**Goal.** Build one `exportChart(rootElement, opts)` helper that captures the **full** rendered figure — including HTML legends, captions, ranking panels, and multi-SVG facet grids — into either PNG or SVG. Then drop the existing `chartDownloadMenu` PNG path in favour of it.

**Current pain (in `obs_month_overlay.qmd`):**

- `_chartDownloadMenu_svgToPng` finds the *first* SVG inside the chartElement and serialises only that one. Multi-SVG grids (Period maps choropleth, Period polar SSP small-multiples, P2/P4 facets) export with only one cell visible.
- HTML siblings (legends, captions, ranking panels) sit *next to* the SVG, not inside it → never appear in the export.
- `chartDownloadMenu` doesn't auto-detect "composite element" vs "single SVG" — same code path for both.

**Design.** Two strategies, picked automatically by the helper:

1. **`composite-foreignObject`** (default for mixed-content / multi-SVG roots). Clone the entire `rootElement` (with computed styles inlined) into an `<svg><foreignObject>` envelope, then rasterise via `<img>` + `<canvas>` → PNG. SVG export emits the foreignObject SVG directly. Captures legends, multi-SVG grids, ranking panels, captions — anything the DOM contains.
2. **`single-svg`** (when the root IS a single SVG or contains exactly one SVG with no HTML siblings of interest). Uses the existing serialise → image → canvas path; simpler + smaller files.

**Acceptance**: the four test cases below all export PNG+SVG visibly identical to what the page shows.

```{ojs}
import { loaderDiv } from "/helpers/uiComponents.ojs";
```

```{ojs}
// chartDownloadMenu is the working PNG/SVG/CSV split-button from the
// main sandbox. We reuse its UI verbatim and only extend its PNG path
// for composite cases via the existing `pngOverride` hook.
import { chartDownloadMenu } from "/helpers/chartDownloadMenu.ojs";
```

```{ojs}
//| output: false
// html-to-image lazy-loaded from esm.sh — used by composite test cases
// via `pngOverride`. OJS awaits the import; `htmlToImageMod.toBlob` is
// usable from any cell after this one resolves.
htmlToImageMod = import("https://esm.sh/html-to-image@1.11.13")
```

```{ojs}
//| output: false
// Helper used by composite cases: rasterises the entire rootElement
// (multi-SVG grid, SVG + HTML legend, pure-HTML table) via html-to-image.
//
// Block-level container quirk: Plot.plot's title renders as an <h2>
// whose border-bottom anchors at the parent's full width, so any
// block-level wrapper around a Plot.plot chart bloats out to fill its
// page column — and html-to-image then captures that column width.
// Toggling the rootElement to display:inline-block immediately before
// capture forces shrink-to-fit, restored in `finally` so the page
// view doesn't reflow visibly.
compositePng = (rootElement) => async () => {
  const prevDisplay = rootElement.style.display;
  rootElement.style.display = "inline-block";
  try {
    return await htmlToImageMod.toBlob(rootElement, {
      pixelRatio: 2,
      backgroundColor: "#ffffff",
      cacheBust: true,
    });
  } finally {
    rootElement.style.display = prevDisplay;
  }
}
```

## Test case 1 — single Plot.plot chart (baseline / regression check)

The simplest case. `chartDownloadMenu` already handles this. Verify the new helper produces the same output.

```{ojs}
//| output: false
tc1 = {
  const data = d3.range(0, 50).map(i => ({ x: i, y: Math.sin(i / 5) + 0.02 * i }));
  return Plot.plot({
    width: 520,
    height: 280,
    title: "Single SVG — sin(x) with drift",
    marks: [
      Plot.ruleY([0], { stroke: "#999", strokeDasharray: "3 3" }),
      Plot.line(data, { x: "x", y: "y", stroke: "#216" }),
      Plot.dot(data, { x: "x", y: "y", r: 2, fill: "#216" }),
    ],
  });
}
```

```{ojs}
// TC1 — single Plot.plot output. chartDownloadMenu's default SVG path
// handles it: PNG via SVG-rasterise, SVG via direct serialise.
tc1_dl = chartDownloadMenu(tc1, { filename: "tc1_single_svg" })
```

## Test case 2 — multi-SVG facet grid

Multiple SVGs inside a flexbox container. Current helper captures one cell only.

```{ojs}
//| output: false
tc2 = {
  const data = d3.range(0, 50);
  const oneCell = (label, phase) => {
    const cell = Plot.plot({
      width: 200, height: 140, marginLeft: 30,
      title: label,
      marks: [
        Plot.ruleY([0], { stroke: "#999", strokeDasharray: "3 3" }),
        Plot.line(data.map(i => ({ x: i, y: Math.sin(i / 5 + phase) })),
                  { x: "x", y: "y", stroke: "#216" }),
      ],
    });
    return cell;
  };
  return htl.html`<div style="display:grid;grid-template-columns:repeat(3, 1fr);gap:8px;background:#fff;padding:8px;">
    ${oneCell("Cell 1 (phase 0)",   0)}
    ${oneCell("Cell 2 (phase π/2)", Math.PI / 2)}
    ${oneCell("Cell 3 (phase π)",   Math.PI)}
    ${oneCell("Cell 4 (phase 3π/2)", 3 * Math.PI / 2)}
    ${oneCell("Cell 5 (phase 2π)",  2 * Math.PI)}
    ${oneCell("Cell 6 (phase 5π/2)", 5 * Math.PI / 2)}
  </div>`;
}
```

```{ojs}
// TC2 — multi-SVG facet grid. Default findSvg() would grab only the
// first cell; route PNG through html-to-image, suppress SVG (composite
// SVG export not reliable enough for this shape).
tc2_dl = chartDownloadMenu(tc2, {
  filename: "tc2_facet_grid_6_cells",
  pngOverride: compositePng(tc2),
  disableSvg: true,
})
```

## Test case 3 — SVG + HTML legend (Period-maps-shaped)

A chart with an HTML legend below it (like Period maps' colour-ramp legend + stipple note). Current helper exports the chart SVG only; the legend goes missing.

```{ojs}
//| output: false
tc3 = {
  const data = d3.range(0, 80).map(i => ({
    x: i % 20, y: Math.floor(i / 20),
    v: Math.sin(i / 5) + Math.cos(i / 7),
  }));
  const chart = Plot.plot({
    width: 520, height: 240, marginLeft: 30,
    title: "Heatmap with external HTML legend",
    color: { scheme: "RdBu", reverse: true, domain: [-2, 2] },
    marks: [
      Plot.cell(data, { x: "x", y: "y", fill: "v" }),
    ],
  });
  // Bespoke HTML legend — what would be lost from a single-SVG export.
  const legendHtml = htl.html`<div style="margin-top:10px;font-size:11px;color:#444;">
    <div style="display:flex;align-items:center;gap:10px;">
      <span style="font-weight:700;">Anomaly (units):</span>
      <span style="display:inline-block;width:140px;height:10px;background:linear-gradient(to right, #2166ac, #f7f7f7, #b2182b);"></span>
      <span>-2</span>
      <span style="opacity:0.6;">0</span>
      <span>+2</span>
    </div>
    <div style="margin-top:4px;color:#777;font-style:italic;">
      Source: synthetic data for download-framework testing.
    </div>
  </div>`;
  return htl.html`<div style="background:#fff;padding:8px;border:1px solid #eee;">
    ${chart}
    ${legendHtml}
  </div>`;
}
```

```{ojs}
// TC3 — SVG + HTML legend wrapper. Default path would export the SVG
// only, dropping the legend. html-to-image PNG captures both.
tc3_dl = chartDownloadMenu(tc3, {
  filename: "tc3_chart_plus_html_legend",
  pngOverride: compositePng(tc3),
  disableSvg: true,
})
```

## Test case 4 — pure HTML (Period-table-shaped)

A heat-mapped table — no SVG anywhere. Must rasterise via foreignObject. Current helper fails entirely (no SVG → no PNG).

```{ojs}
//| output: false
tc4 = {
  const rows = ["A","B","C","D"];
  const cols = ["2021-2040","2041-2060","2061-2080","2081-2100"];
  const cellVal = (r, c) => Math.sin((r + c) / 3) * 2;
  const shade = v => {
    const t = (v + 2) / 4;
    return `rgba(${Math.round(216 * (1 - t) + 31 * t)}, 117, ${Math.round(48 * (1 - t) + 180 * t)}, 0.6)`;
  };
  const th = "padding:6px 12px;background:#f3f3f3;border-bottom:2px solid #888;font-size:0.85em;text-align:center;";
  const td = "padding:6px 12px;border-bottom:1px solid #eee;font-size:0.9em;text-align:center;";
  return htl.html`<div style="background:#fff;padding:8px;">
    <p style="margin:0 0 6px;font-weight:600;color:#222;">Test 4: pure HTML heat-mapped table</p>
    <table style="border-collapse:collapse;">
      <thead><tr><th style="${th}">Row</th>${cols.map(c => htl.html`<th style="${th}">${c}</th>`)}</tr></thead>
      <tbody>${rows.map((r, ri) => htl.html`<tr>
        <td style="${td};font-weight:600;background:#f6f6f6;">${r}</td>
        ${cols.map((c, ci) => {
          const v = cellVal(ri, ci);
          return htl.html`<td style="${td};background:${shade(v)};">${(v >= 0 ? "+" : "") + v.toFixed(2)}</td>`;
        })}
      </tr>`)}</tbody>
    </table>
  </div>`;
}
```

```{ojs}
//| output: false
// TC4's row-major data — enables the CSV menu item below.
tc4_data = {
  const rows = ["A","B","C","D"];
  const cols = ["2021-2040","2041-2060","2061-2080","2081-2100"];
  return rows.flatMap((r, ri) =>
    cols.map((c, ci) => ({ row: r, period: c, value: Math.sin((ri + ci) / 3) * 2 })));
}
```

```{ojs}
// TC4 — pure HTML. No SVG → default chartDownloadMenu PNG would be
// disabled; pngOverride wires html-to-image.
tc4_dl = chartDownloadMenu(tc4, {
  filename: "tc4_pure_html_table",
  data: tc4_data,
  pngOverride: compositePng(tc4),
  disableSvg: true,
})
```

## Test case 5 — SVG composite with d3 (polar-clock-shaped)

A single SVG, but containing multiple `<g>` subgraphs at calculated positions — mimics Period polar's grid-inside-one-SVG layout.

```{ojs}
//| output: false
tc5 = {
  const cellW = 200, cellH = 200, nCols = 3, nRows = 2;
  const totalW = cellW * nCols + 30, totalH = cellH * nRows + 50;
  const svg = d3.create("svg")
    .attr("viewBox", `0 0 ${totalW} ${totalH}`)
    .attr("width", totalW).attr("height", totalH)
    .style("font-family", "system-ui, sans-serif")
    .style("background", "#fff");
  svg.append("text").attr("x", totalW / 2).attr("y", 16)
    .attr("text-anchor", "middle").attr("font-size", 12).attr("font-weight", 600)
    .text("Test 5: 6-cell SVG composite (one root SVG, multiple <g> subgraphs)");
  for (let r = 0; r < nRows; r++) for (let c = 0; c < nCols; c++) {
    const cxCell = 15 + c * cellW + cellW / 2;
    const cyCell = 30 + r * cellH + cellH / 2;
    const g = svg.append("g").attr("transform", `translate(${cxCell}, ${cyCell})`);
    // Radial bars per "month" with phase per cell.
    for (let m = 0; m < 12; m++) {
      const angle = (m / 12) * 2 * Math.PI - Math.PI / 2;
      const v = 30 + 30 * Math.sin(m / 2 + r * 0.7 + c * 0.5);
      g.append("line")
        .attr("x1", 0).attr("y1", 0)
        .attr("x2", Math.cos(angle) * v).attr("y2", Math.sin(angle) * v)
        .attr("stroke", d3.interpolateInferno(0.2 + 0.7 * (m / 11)))
        .attr("stroke-width", 4).attr("stroke-linecap", "round");
    }
    g.append("text").attr("y", -75).attr("text-anchor", "middle")
      .attr("font-size", 10).attr("font-weight", 600).text(`Cell ${r * nCols + c + 1}`);
  }
  return svg.node();
}
```

```{ojs}
// TC5 — single bare SVG with internal <g> subgraphs. chartDownloadMenu's
// default path serialises the whole SVG, so all subgraphs are kept.
tc5_dl = chartDownloadMenu(tc5, { filename: "tc5_single_svg_composite" })
```

## The framework — reuse the working `chartDownloadMenu`

Earlier iterations tried to ship a parallel `exportBar` helper. Each
form hit the same OJS-binding tarpit (`.ojs` module → "exportDataCsvV2
is not defined"; in-cell function expression → "invalid binding";
combined dropdown wired around dynamic `htl.html` buttons → same).

Pete's correct call: the existing `chartDownloadMenu` already exposes a
single split-button with **PNG / SVG / CSV** and is proven in the main
sandbox. Its `pngOverride` hook is exactly the extension point this
test sandbox needs — it lets composite cases route PNG through
`html-to-image` while keeping the existing UI. `disableSvg` suppresses
the SVG menu item for composites where a single-SVG serialisation
would be lossy.

The test cases above call `chartDownloadMenu` directly — no new helper
required. The only new code is the lazy `html-to-image` import and the
`compositePng(rootElement)` factory near the top of the page, both of
which sit in their own cells.

---

## What to verify in the rendered page

For each of the 5 test cases:

1. Each test case renders the chart followed by the standard `chartDownloadMenu` split-button (primary "Download PNG" + caret ▾ for "Download as SVG" / "Download data (CSV)").
2. **TC1 (Plot.plot single SVG)** — PNG and SVG buttons both download a clean file matching the rendered figure. CSV disabled (no data passed).
3. **TC2 (multi-SVG facet grid)** — PNG includes **all six cells**, not just the first. SVG button disabled (composite SVG not reliable). CSV disabled.
4. **TC3 (SVG + HTML legend)** — PNG includes the **legend below the chart**, not just the heatmap SVG. SVG disabled. CSV disabled.
5. **TC4 (pure HTML table)** — PNG renders the **full table** (heading, header row, all four data rows). SVG disabled (no source SVG). CSV **enabled** — downloads a 16-row UTF-8 BOM file.
6. **TC5 (single SVG composite)** — PNG and SVG both capture all six `<g>` subgraphs.

If any case fails: open DevTools → console; `html-to-image` logs verbose errors there. Paste back here.

Once the five test cases pass, promote the pattern:

1. Add a real `compositePng` helper to `helpers/chartDownloadMenu.ojs` (named export) so callers don't reinvent the `htmlToImageMod.toBlob(…)` wrapper at every site.
2. Sweep `obs_month_overlay.qmd` sections whose `chartDownloadMenu(…)` currently exports only the first inner SVG — Period maps, Period polar SSP grid, Period table, P2 / P4 facets, P6 grid — pass `pngOverride: compositePng(chart)` + `disableSvg: true` for the composite ones.
3. Verify in the live notebook: PNG outputs match the rendered figures.
